With reference to the financial relations between the Union and the States in India, which of the following statements are correct?

A. The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year or even earlier to recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes to be shared between the Centre and the states, the allocation between the states and the respective shares of such proceeds.

q: Who is the highest law officer of the country?
explanation: The Attorney General of India (Art. 76) is the highest law officer of the country; the CJI heads the judiciary and the PM the executive.

notes.text: - **Attorney General (AG) of India** = the **highest law officer** of the country and the **first law officer / chief legal adviser** of the **Government of India** (Art. 76).

q: Which one of the following is a qualification for a person to be appointed as Attorney General of India?
options: He shall be an advocate of standing
He shall be qualified to be appointed as a Judge of Supreme Court
He shall be a retired judge of Supreme Court
key_text: He shall be qualified to be appointed as a Judge of Supreme Court
explanation: Art. 76(1): the AG must be qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court – not merely 'an advocate of standing', a jurist, or a retired SC judge.

options: Qualified to be appointed as a High Court Judge
Qualified to be appointed as a Supreme Court Judge
Any eminent person with legal background
key_text: Qualified to be appointed as a Supreme Court Judge
explanation: Art. 76(1): the AG must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge; the High Court-judge qualification applies to the Advocate General.

notes.text: - Must be **qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court** – not merely a High Court judge, "any advocate" or "a retired SC judge".

q: Even though he is not a member of the House, out of the persons below who can participate in the proceedings of Lok Sabha?
explanation: Under Art. 88 the Attorney General can take part in Lok Sabha proceedings though not a member; the Solicitor General, CJI and Vice-President cannot.

notes.text: - The AG has the right to **speak and otherwise take part** in the proceedings of **both Houses**, their **joint sitting** and **any parliamentary committee of which he is named a member** – **without being an MP**.
- **Only the AG** among the listed officers has this right: **not** the Solicitor General, CJI, CEC, CAG, Finance Commission chairman, NHRC chairman or National Security Adviser.

q: Attorney-General of India has the right to audience in
options: Any Court of law within the territory of India
key_text: Any Court of law within the territory of India
explanation: Art. 76(3): the AG has the right of audience in any court of law within the territory of India – not only the SC, a High Court or a Sessions court.

notes.text: - **Right of audience in all courts in the territory of India** – not only the Supreme Court, not only High Courts or Sessions courts.

q: Advocate-General of a State is the first law officer of a State and is appointed by
explanation: Art. 165(1): the Advocate General, the first law officer of the State, is appointed by the Governor – not the President, PM or Supreme Court.

notes.text: - **Resigns** to the **President**; **by convention** (not by the Constitution) he resigns when the Council of Ministers resigns or is replaced (UPSC 2022: "the Constitution requires him to resign with the government" = wrong).

q: An official corresponding post to the Attorney General of India at the State level is
explanation: The Advocate General (Art. 165) is the State counterpart of the Attorney General (Art. 76) – the highest law officer and legal adviser of the State Government.

notes.text: - **No fixed term** in the Constitution; **no grounds or procedure for removal**; holds office **during the pleasure of the President** – not the PM, not Parliament. So "the President cannot remove the AG" is **wrong**.

q: The remuneration of an Advocate General would be

Equal to that of the Chief Secretary of the State
Equal to that of the Cabinet Minister of the State
explanation: The Advocate General receives such remuneration as the Governor may determine (Art. 165(3)); it is not tied to the pay of an HC judge, Chief Secretary or minister.

notes.text: - 1. **Advise the Government of India** on legal matters **referred by the President**.

q:
Which of the following statements about the Attorney General of India is/are correct?

I. The President shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney General of India.

II. He shall have right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.

III. He shall hold office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister.

IV. He receives remuneration as determined by Parliament.
explanation: I and II are correct: the President appoints a person qualified to be an SC judge, and the AG has right of audience in all courts. III and IV are wrong: he holds office during the pleasure of the President and his remuneration is fixed by the President, not Parliament.
